questions.question: Find the synonym of 'Hamstrung'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Cripple**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Hamstrung"** means to severely restrict the efficiency or effectiveness of someone or something; it also refers to being crippled or hindered. (अक्षम करना / पंगु बनाना)
 
 
 
• **Example:** The new rules hamstrung the company’s ability to innovate and expand.
 
 
 
• The word **"Cripple"** has a similar meaning, referring to causing severe damage or hindrance to something or someone, making them less effective. (पंगु बनाना)
 
 
 
• **Example:** The lack of funding crippled the project, halting it midway.
 
 
 
• Thus, **"Cripple"** is the synonym of **"Hamstrung."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Cripple**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Talkative** (बातूनी): Someone who talks a lot or is overly chatty.
 
 
 
• **Example:** She is so talkative that she can keep a conversation going for hours.
 
 
 
• **Jolly** (मज़ाकिया / प्रसन्नचित्त): Someone who is cheerful, full of good humor, or happy.
 
 
 
• **Example:** He was in a jolly mood after hearing the good news.
 
 
 
• **Restless** (बेचैन): Unable to stay still or calm, often due to anxiety or impatience.
 
 
 
• **Example:** The children were restless as they waited for the results of their performance.

Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
'By fits and starts'
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. With breaks**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"By fits and starts"** means to do something irregularly or intermittently, with periods of activity followed by inactivity. (रुक-रुक कर)
 
 
• **Example:** He has been working on his project by fits and starts, so it's taking much longer to complete.
 
 
• Here, the correct meaning of the idiom aligns with **"With breaks"**, which means something that is done in a non-continuous manner. (रुकावटों के साथ)
 
 
• **Example:** The team completed the task with breaks, which led to delays in the project.
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "By fits and starts" means **"With breaks."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. With breaks**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: Quickly** (तेजी से) – Refers to something done in a fast or swift manner.
 
 
• **Example:** She quickly finished her homework before going out to play.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Smoothly** (स्मूदली) – Refers to something done without any interruptions or difficulties.
 
 
• **Example:** The event went smoothly, with no technical glitches.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Forever** (हमेशा के लिए) – Refers to something that lasts for an infinite or very long period of time.

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

He has written a novel inspired by his time spent in rural India.

options.text: A novel inspired by his time spent in rural India had been written by him.
A novel inspired by his time spent in rural India is written by him.
A novel inspired by his time spent in rural India has been written by him.
A novel inspired by his time spent in rural India was written by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive Voice Transformation:** When converting from active to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense** (Active: *has/have + past participle*).
 
• The structure for **Present Perfect Passive** is: **Object + has/have + been + Past Participle + (by + Subject)**.
 
• **Step-by-step conversion:** 
 
 
• **Active Subject:** "He" (becomes "him" in the by-phrase).
 
• **Active Verb:** "has written".
 
• **Active Object:** "a novel inspired by his time spent in rural India".
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A novel inspired by his time spent in rural India has been written by him."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "...had been written..." – This is the **Past Perfect Passive** tense, which implies a past action completed before another past action.
 
• **Option 2:** "...is written..." – This is the **Simple Present Passive** tense, typically used for general facts or habits.
 
• **Option 4:** "...was written..." – This is the **Simple Past Passive** tense, used for completed actions in the past.

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

They will have finalized the agenda by tomorrow morning.

options.text: The agenda had been finalized by them.
The agenda was finalized by them.
The agenda will have been finalized by tomorrow morning.
The agenda will be finalized tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Future Perfect tense** in the active voice ("**will have finalized**").
 
• To convert Future Perfect from active to passive, the structure used is: **Object + will have + been + past participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• The object "**the agenda**" becomes the new subject, and "**will have finalized**" changes to "**will have been finalized**."
 
• Option 3 is the only choice that maintains the correct tense and follows the passive voice formula for the future perfect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The **agenda will have been finalized** by tomorrow morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Past Perfect Passive):** "had been finalized" is used when the original sentence is in the past perfect tense.
 
• **Option 2 (Simple Past Passive):** "was finalized" is used for converting sentences originally in the simple past tense.
 
• **Option 4 (Simple Future Passive):** "will be finalized" is the passive form for the simple future ("will finalize").

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

He said to me, "Please wait here till I come back."

options.text: He requested me to wait there till he came back.
He told me to please wait there.
He asked that I waited till he comes back.
He asked I should wait until he comes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He requested me to wait there till he came back.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The word **"Please"** in the direct speech indicates a request. Therefore, the reporting verb **"said to"** changes to **"requested."**
 
 
 
• **Imperative Structure:**
 
 
• In imperative sentences (commands or requests), the conjunction **"to"** is used before the base form of the verb. Thus, "wait" becomes the infinitive **"to wait."**
 
 
 
• **Time and Place Words:**
 
 
• The demonstrative adverb of place **"here"** changes to **"there"** in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun and Tense Changes (in the dependent clause):**
 
 
• The first-person pronoun **"I"** changes to the third-person **"he"** to match the speaker.
 
• Because the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the simple present verb **"come"** changes to the simple past **"came."**
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He requested me to wait there till he came back."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He told me to please wait there."

 
 
• Incorrect because the word "please" should be omitted in indirect speech; its meaning is already conveyed by changing the reporting verb to "requested." It also misses the second half of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He asked that I waited till he comes back."
 
 
• Incorrect grammatical structure. Imperative requests use the "to + verb" infinitive structure. It also fails to change the tense of "comes" to "came."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He asked I should wait until he comes."
 
 
• Incorrect structure. The addition of "should" is unnecessary and it fails to change the present tense "comes" to the past tense "came."

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

My friend said, "I can help you with your project."

options.text: My friend said that he could help me with my project.
My friend said that he can help me.
My friend said he would help in project.
My friend said that he may help with project.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** My friend said that he could help me with my project.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I can help" becomes "he could help"**
 
 
• The first-person pronoun **"I"** changes to the third-person **"he"** (or "she") to match the subject of the reporting verb ("My friend").
 
• The modal verb **"can"** changes to its past tense form **"could"** because the reporting verb ("said") is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **"you" becomes "me" and "your" becomes "my"**
 
 
• The second-person object pronoun **"you"** changes to the first-person **"me"** as the speaker is reporting what was said to them.
 
• The possessive adjective **"your"** changes to **"my"** to maintain consistency with the change in the object pronoun.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Clause:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is introduced to connect the reporting clause to the reported statement.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My friend said that he could help me with my project."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "My friend said that he can help me."

 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the tense of the modal **"can"** to **"could,"** and it completely omits the "with your project" part of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "My friend said he would help in project."
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the modal from "can" (expressing ability) to "would" (expressing intention/future), and it drops the necessary pronouns "me" and "my."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "My friend said that he may help with project."
 
 
• Incorrect because it alters the original meaning by replacing "can" (ability) with "may" (possibility) and omits the required object and possessive pronouns.

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

My sister said that she was going to the market.

options.text: My sister said, "I am going to the market."
My sister said, "She is going to the market."
My sister said, "She was going to the market."
My sister said, "I go to the market."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** My sister said that she was going to the market.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"she was going" becomes "I am going"**
 
 
• The third-person pronoun **"she"** changes to the first-person pronoun **"I"** because the speaker (the sister) is referring to herself in direct speech.
 
• The Past Continuous tense (**was going**) correctly reverts to the Present Continuous tense (**am going**) in direct speech because the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Clause:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is removed, and the direct speech is separated from the reporting verb by a comma and enclosed in quotation marks.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct quote is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• It begins with a capital letter and ends with a period inside the quotation marks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *My sister said, "I am going to the market."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** My sister said, "She is going to the market."

 
 
• Incorrect because the pronoun **"She"** is used instead of **"I"**. The speaker would refer to herself as "I".
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** My sister said, "She was going to the market."
 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change both the pronoun and the tense back to the present continuous.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** My sister said, "I go to the market."
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the tense to Simple Present (**"go"**) instead of Present Continuous (**"am going"**), which would mean a general habit rather than an ongoing action.

questions.question:
Transform the following sentence into active voice.

The letter is expected to be delivered by the bearer within the stipulated time.

options.text: They expect the bearer to deliver the letter within the stipulated time.
They expect the letter to deliver the bearer within the stipulated time.
They expect the bearer to deliver the stipulated time within the the letter.
They expect the bearer to delivered the letter within the stipulated time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains two passive structures: "**is expected**" (by an implied subject) and "**to be delivered**" (by the bearer).
 
• To convert to active voice, we introduce a general subject like "**They**" or "People" to perform the action of expecting.
 
• The passive infinitive "**to be delivered**" must be changed to the active infinitive "**to deliver**."
 
• The agent "**the bearer**" becomes the subject of the infinitive phrase, and "**the letter**" becomes the object.
 
• Option 1 correctly follows this logic: **Subject ("They") + verb ("expect") + object/agent ("the bearer") + active infinitive ("to deliver") + object ("the letter")**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **They expect the bearer to deliver the letter within the stipulated time**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They **expect** the **bearer to deliver** the letter within the stipulated time."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** This incorrectly suggests the letter is delivering the person ("deliver the bearer"), which reverses the logical meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** This is nonsensical as it suggests the bearer is delivering "time" inside a "letter."
 
• **Option 4:** This contains a grammatical error; the infinitive marker "to" must be followed by the base form of the verb ("deliver"), not the past participle ("delivered").

questions.question:
Transform the following sentence into active voice.

The roads and bridges that connect many important cities in India have been renovated or rebuilt with great alacrity.

options.text: They have renovated or rebuilt the roads and bridges with great alacrity that connect many important cities.
They have renovated or rebuilt the roads and bridges that connect many important cities with great alacrity in India.
They have renovated or rebuilt the roads and bridges that connect many important cities in India with great alacrity.
They have renovated or rebuilt the roads and bridges that with great alacrity connect many important cities in India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive to Active Voice Conversion:** In this transformation, the object of the passive sentence (which is the recipient of the action) becomes the object of the active sentence, and an agent (like "They") is introduced as the subject.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense**: *"have been renovated or rebuilt."*
 
• The active structure for Present Perfect is: **Subject + has/have + Past Participle + Object**.
 
• The phrase **"with great alacrity"** is an adverbial phrase that modifies the verbs "renovated or rebuilt." In the active voice, it should ideally follow the object it describes to maintain the flow of the original sentence.
 
• The entire noun phrase **"the roads and bridges that connect many important cities in India"** must stay together as the object to avoid "misplaced modifiers" (which happen when a descriptive phrase is too far from the word it describes).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They have renovated or rebuilt the roads and bridges that connect many important cities in India with great alacrity."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Identify the error in the sentence.

We was discussing the project when the lights went out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part 4** of the sentence, specifically regarding **subject-verb agreement**.
 
• In the Past Continuous tense, the auxiliary verb must agree with the subject in number.
 
• The subject "**We**" is a first-person **plural** pronoun.
 
• The verb "**was**" is used for singular subjects (I, He, She, It), whereas "**were**" must be used for plural subjects (We, You, They).
 
• Therefore, "**was**" should be replaced with "**were**" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"We **were** discussing the project when the lights went out."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ("project"):** This is a correct singular noun acting as the object of the verb "discussing."
 
• **Option 2 ("lights"):** This is a correct plural noun acting as the subject of the second clause.
 
• **Option 3 ("discussing"):** This is the correct present participle form used to create the continuous tense.
 
• **Tense Consistency:** The sentence correctly uses the Past Continuous ("were discussing") to show an ongoing action that was interrupted by a finished action in the Simple Past ("went out").

questions.question: Choose the correct one word substitution for: someone who believes their own culture is superior to others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Ethnocentric**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Ethnocentric"** refers to someone who believes their own culture, ethnicity, or nationality is superior to others. (सांस्कृतिक केंद्रित)
 
 
• **Example:** His ethnocentric views made it difficult for him to appreciate the diversity of other cultures.
 
 
• **"Ethnocentric" **is a term commonly used in sociology to describe attitudes that evaluate other cultures based on the standards of one's own culture. (सांस्कृतिक श्रेष्ठता)
 
 
• **Example:** The ethnocentric policies of the regime led to the suppression of minority traditions and languages.
 
 
• The term perfectly captures the essence of the question.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Ethnocentric**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Polymathic** (विविध विद्या में निपुण): Refers to someone who is knowledgeable in many different fields or subjects.
 
 
• **Example:** Leonardo da Vinci is often considered a polymathic genius for his contributions to art, science, and engineering.
 
 

 
• **Cosmopolitan** (सर्वदेशीय): Refers to someone or something that is worldly or at ease with many different cultures.
 
 
• **Example:** New York City is known for its cosmopolitan nature, attracting people from all over the world.
 
 

 
• **Esoteric** (गूढ़): Refers to knowledge or information intended for or likely to be understood by only a small, specialized group of people.
 
 
• **Example:** The professor's lecture on quantum mechanics was highly esoteric and difficult for most students to grasp.
